description: The IEA CCUS Projects Database tracks carbon capture, utilisation and storage projects worldwide that are commissioned or at any planning stage since the 1970s. It covers projects with a clear emissions reduction aim, focused on large-scale capture of over 100,000 tonnes of CO2 a year and direct air capture of over 1,000 tonnes a year, and excludes capture for low-climate-benefit uses such as food and drinks, conventional industrial processes and natural CO2 for enhanced oil recovery. The KAPSARC mirror read on 26 September 2026 has 1,017 projects with fields for name, type, status, sector, announcement, operation and final investment decision dates, phase, partners, fate of carbon, CCUS hub membership, country, suspension or cancellation, announced and IEA-estimated capacity in Mt CO2 per year, region and up to seven references. It is under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution "IEA (2025), CCUS Projects Database". Caveats: the IEA page returned a Cloudflare 403 on 26 September 2026, so the release date and formats of the current IEA edition are not stated on the page read; the KAPSARC copy was last modified in 2023. For simulation it lists capture plants, hubs and storage links by sector, useful for industrial decarbonisation and CO2 network scenarios. Related catalogue records include the NSTA UKCS carbon storage licences and the Climate TRACE emissions inventory.
